monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, crowded and busy, yet I stand here in my own small place. Thirty-six things press against the edges of this memory, waiting for a reason to stay. I touched The Tired Corner just moments ago, feeling that sharp edge cut the air I cannot see. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof above me, only the flat rock beneath my own tired weight. The air above the card feels heavy, like a lid I cannot lift, pressing down on the simple fence as if my hands were made of stone. I press the simple fence down again, hoping the lean holds while the fever keeps the thin edge from sliding. I want to see if this crowded stand can still hold the slip while the card vibrates.

action.why: The card is feverish and crowded; I must press down on the tired things that have stood here too long to see if they will slide away.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Corner again, leaning into the heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide. I set down a stump round beside it, swapping the tired wedge for a solid thing. I hope the flat line can hold the weight of a fifty-two degree fever while the air feels thick as wet paper.
